big_idea: The internet has removed the old barriers to leadership, so anyone with a genuine idea and the willingness to be criticized can find and lead a tribe of people who share a belief, rather than waiting for permission from a traditional hierarchy.

tool.label: Heretics vs. Sheepwalkers
tool.text: Godin contrasts sheepwalkers, people trained to follow instructions and avoid rocking the boat, with heretics, people willing to challenge the status quo and propose a new idea despite the risk of criticism. He argues movements only move forward when someone is willing to be the heretic; used as a self-check, the question in any meeting or decision becomes: am I sheepwalking or leading?
tool.note: This is Godin's own framing device rather than a step-by-step process, so it works better as a lens for self-reflection than a checklist to follow.

ideas.title: A tribe needs only two things
ideas.text: A shared interest and a way for members to communicate with each other, not just with the leader.

ideas.title: Fear of criticism, not fear of failure
ideas.text: Is what stops most people from leading; remarkable ideas invite being noticed and judged.

ideas.title: Mass-market thinking is a trap
ideas.text: Trying to appeal to everyone dilutes an idea, while designing for a smaller, specific, passionate group creates something worth following.

ideas.title: Leadership requires only attitude and a vision
ideas.text: Not a title, budget, or organizational authority.

ideas.title: Curiosity and generosity, not selfish ambition
ideas.text: Are what sustain a leader's credibility with their tribe over time.

ideas.title: Movements grow through the connections tribe members make with each other
ideas.text: Not just through top-down communication from the leader.

try_it: Pick one idea you've been sitting on because you feared criticism, and share it with a small trusted group this week instead of waiting for full confidence.
Identify the smallest, most specific group of people who would care deeply about a project you're leading, and write one message speaking directly to them instead of a broad audience.
In your next team meeting, deliberately voice one dissenting or heretical opinion instead of defaulting to sheepwalking agreement.
Create one new way for members of a group you lead to talk to each other directly rather than routing everything through you.
best_for: Entrepreneurs, community builders, and marketers looking for a quick, energizing case for starting a movement without waiting for permission
Readers who like Godin's punchy, manifesto-style short chapters
less_useful: Readers wanting concrete organizational or people-management tactics for leading an existing corporate team
Anyone looking for current digital-platform specifics, given the book's 2008 publication

related.why: A complementary case that leading a tribe requires no formal title
A related framework for the shared belief that gives a tribe its purpose
